headline: Funding flows. Contracts expand. Plans explode.
deck: This week, funding rounds and contract modifications signal a busy space economy, but not without its hiccups.

stories.head: Iceye raises €1 billion for satellite expansion
stories.body: Iceye secured over €1 billion to enhance its synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite systems, illustrating the appetite for high-resolution imaging in a competitive market. This funding round underscores the trend of large capital influxes into satellite technology, with investors eager to capitalize on the growing demand for Earth observation data.
stories.soWhat: When investors throw around billions, it's a sign that they believe the satellite game is about to get a lot more crowded—and potentially messy.

stories.head: BlackSky accelerates reconnaissance under NRO contract
stories.body: BlackSky received a contract modification from the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) to expedite its broad-area collection satellites. This modification aims to enhance the speed and efficiency of reconnaissance operations, a clear signal that the government prioritizes timely intelligence in an increasingly complex global landscape.
stories.soWhat: In the world of reconnaissance, faster satellites might just mean a faster path to the next geopolitical crisis.

stories.head: Warren AI launches risk analysis engine for space
stories.body: Warren AI™ has rolled out its risk analysis engine aimed at the burgeoning space economy, emphasizing the need for risk management in a sector rife with uncertainties. As space ventures grow in number and complexity, this tool could become essential for navigating potential pitfalls.
stories.soWhat: If space is the new frontier, then managing risk is the new frontier's necessary evil—because cosmic catastrophes have a way of making headlines.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Iceye's expansion plans
watchlist.body: With €1 billion in hand, Iceye's next moves could reshape the SAR landscape—watch for potential partnerships or acquisitions.

watchlist.title: BlackSky's speed could attract more contracts
watchlist.body: If BlackSky can deliver on its accelerated timeline, expect other agencies to take note and possibly follow suit with their own contracts.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's Series C impacts defense procurement
watchlist.body: With $190 million raised, True Anomaly may become a key player in co-orbital security—defense contracts could follow.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension on the TITAN program suggests that established players can maintain dominance through government contracts, potentially stifling newcomers.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
